title: Frame store has no writer lock: concurrent appends lose data and rollback can delete in-flight work
description: append_frame_shard_h5() checks file.exists(final) then commits with file.rename(), which silently replaces the target, so two interleaved appends both report success and the root manifest loses one writer's observations; overwrite = FALSE in write_frame_h5() has the same check-then-act race. recover_frame_store(action = 'rollback') deletes temporary-looking artifacts with no proof the writer is gone, so it can delete a shard published before its manifest commit or an in-flight write_frame_h5() partial. Needs a lock or lease file held across read-manifest -> commit, honoured by rollback, and publication with file.link() (fails if target exists). Repros: scratch review-frame e06/e07/e08 (concurrency emulated with trace()).

title: read_dataset() cannot read LatentNeuroVec files
description: Auto-detection classifies .lv.h5 files as H5NeuroVecSeq (they have /header and /scans) and errors 'Invalid NeuroVecSeq HDF5 file'. read_dataset(type = 'LatentNeuroVec') builds basis from t(/basis/basis_matrix) and loadings from t(embedding) (swapped), ignores sparse bases and the transform, and errors. Detect via the rtype / latent_spec_version attributes before the heuristics and delegate to load_data(LatentNeuroVecSource(file)) (R/read_dataset_methods.R ~140 and ~267-333).
close_reason: detect_h5_type() checks rtype/latent_spec_version before the H5NeuroVecSeq heuristic, and read_dataset(type = 'LatentNeuroVec') delegates to load_data(LatentNeuroVecSource(file)); regression test in test-vec-regressions.R

title: H5NeuroVecSeq can never load a file written by neurovecseq_to_h5()
description: H5NeuroVecSeq() opens the file read-only and then constructs each scan with H5NeuroVec(), which reopens it in mode 'a' and fails ('file is already open for read-only'). Even without that, H5NeuroVec() requires rtype DenseNeuroVec and a 4-D /space/dim that neurovecseq_to_h5() does not write, and detect_h5_type() labels these files H5NeuroVol. Build each scan's H5NeuroVec with new() on the shared handle and NeuroSpace(c(dim3, n_time), trans = ...), and map rtype 'NeuroVecSeq' in detection (R/h5neurovecseq.R ~20-31).

title: Upstream: concat(LatentNeuroVec, DenseNeuroVol) fails on a matrix orientation mismatch
description: The one remaining failing test (test_latent_vec_concat.R 'concat handles mixed object types...') is an upstream bug: as(LatentNeuroVec, 'matrix') is inherited from neuroim2's AbstractSparseNeuroVec and returns time x masked-voxels (8 x 140), while DenseNeuroVol/DenseNeuroVec coerce to all-voxels x time (144 x 1), so neuroim2's .concat4D() cbind()s mismatched matrices. Fix belongs in fmrilatent (a concat(LatentNeuroVec, NeuroVol) method or a voxels x time coercion) or neuroim2's .concat4D(). fmristore defines no concat method; keep the test failing until upstream is fixed.

title: CI lint gate cannot pass: cyclocomp missing and 5,631 existing lints
description: lint.yaml runs lintr::lint_package() with LINTR_ERROR_ON_LINT=true. Current lintr no longer bundles cyclocomp, and the workflow installs only lintr, so cyclocomp_linter aborts lint_package() before any lint is reported. With cyclocomp installed the configured tags report 5,631 lints in 65 files (implicit_integer_linter 3,850, condition_call_linter 406, namespace_linter 342, undesirable_function_linter 172, ...). Decide whether to relax .lintr (e.g. drop implicit_integer/condition_call) or restyle, and add any::cyclocomp to the workflow. The style workflow is red for the same kind of pre-existing debt.

title: h5_array_source fingerprint is never validated when a source is opened
description: source_open() never checks the stored dims, dtype or fingerprint, and the fingerprint uses file size plus one-second mtime, so rewriting a file with same-size content within a second leaves an old descriptor silently reading new values. Validate shape/dtype/fingerprint in source_open() and use sub-second mtime or a commit token (R/array_source.R ~108-120, ~242-253).

title: Frame commits do not fsync and hide close errors before rename
description: write_frame_h5() and the shard writers flush and close via close_h5_safely(), which swallows close errors with try(silent = TRUE), then rename. Nothing fsyncs the file or parent directory, so after power loss or ENOSPC a truncated file can sit under the committed name. Close without try() on the commit path and fsync file and directory.

title: Cluster label 0 is accepted by writers but rejected by readers
description: A full write with label 0 inside the mask succeeds, but any read touching that voxel errors ('Cluster ID must be positive'), including a whole-volume subset; summary writes fail because the writer's ID set includes 0 and summarize_by_clusters() excludes it. Either reject 0 labels at write time or treat 0 as background everywhere, using one ID set in every writer (R/io_write_h5.R, R/write_dataset_methods.R ~28/65, R/cluster_array.R ~215).

title: H5ParcellatedScan x[i] means mask indices or x coordinates depending on the values
description: x[i] is treated as mask indices only when every value is <= n_voxels and otherwise as first-axis coordinates, so on a 20x2x1 volume with 3 mask voxels run[c(1,3)] is 2x4 while run[c(1,4)] is 2x2x4. Pick one meaning for a single subscript (series() already takes mask indices) and error when out of range (R/cluster_array.R ~244-258).

title: LabeledVolumeSet never sets its space slot
description: read_labeled_vec() constructs the object without a 4-D space, so dim(lvs) is integer(0), series(lvs, 5L) errors, and lvs[2] returns a 3x2x3 slab rather than a linear value. Pass NeuroSpace(c(dim3, n_labels), ...) to new() (R/labeled_vec.R ~521-527).

title: H5NeuroVec/H5NeuroVol constructors open files writable and leak on validation errors
description: Both constructors open in mode 'a' although documented read-only, and leave the handle open when validation fails; write_labeled_vec() truncates the file before validating dtype, so an invalid call destroys the file and keeps it locked until gc(). Validate before opening, close on error via on.exit, open readers with mode 'r' (R/h5neurovec.R ~76-90, R/labeled_vec.R ~147-178).

title: write_parcellated_scan_h5() writes cluster metadata where the experiment reader does not look
description: It writes metadata columns to /clusters/<col> instead of /clusters/cluster_meta/ and writes no summary_only or class attributes, so H5ParcellatedMultiScan() opens its files with an empty cluster_metadata. The summary writer also does not check metadata n_time against nrow. Align with ClusteredTimeSeriesSpec.yaml and the io_write_h5.R layout.

title: Single-timepoint inputs fail in write_cluster_result() and summarize_by_clusters()
description: With a 1-timepoint NeuroVec both modes fail with 'subscript out of bounds' because series() drops to a vector in summarize_by_clusters()/extract_cluster_data(); summarize_by_clusters() also forces na.rm = TRUE so summary_fun = function(x) max(x) errors. write_cluster_result() additionally passes cluster_metadata = NULL through ..., so write_dataset() skips its default metadata (read-back is a 0x0 data.frame) and the dots cleanup is dead code.

title: write_dataset(LatentNeuroVec, 'x.h5') writes 'x.h5.lv.h5'; write_dataset on a to_nih5_vec() handle copies an unflushed file
description: to_h5_latentvec() appends '.lv.h5' to any name not already ending in it, so an explicit path is not honoured. write_dataset() on the handle returned by to_nih5_vec() (still open in 'w', unflushed) file.copy()s an unreadable file; flush before copying (R/write_dataset_methods.R).

title: Frame manifests are R-serialized and unserialize()d from files
description: Semantic and storage manifests are stored as serialize() output and read back with unserialize(), which executes no code by itself but trusts arbitrary object graphs (e.g. promises, environments with active bindings) from any file a user opens. Consider a schema'd format (JSON/HDF5 attributes) for FDS manifests.

title: series(H5NeuroVec, drop = FALSE) ignores drop; H5NeuroVol[, , ] returns a flat vector
description: series(h, 5, drop = FALSE) returns a vector where DenseNeuroVec returns 5x1 (callGeneric drops the argument, R/h5neurovec.R ~380). H5NeuroVol[, , ] inherits neuroim2's ArrayLike3D method and returns a flat vector instead of an array.

title: Frame dtype accounting: float16/bfloat16 sizing, NA in float32, native read types
description: .h5_dtype_bytes() counts float16/bfloat16 as 2 bytes but the codec stores them as 4-byte floats, so chunk budgets and read-plan bytes under-count 2x; memory_budget counts dtype bytes rather than realized R bytes. float32 stores NA as NaN. h5_array_source returns hdf5r's native R type, so uint8/int16 assays read back as integer while fmridataset treats them as double (equal values, not identical()).

title: Remove duplicated code paths
description: as_h5(NeuroVecSeq) (R/io_h5_generic.R ~88-210) copies neurovecseq_to_h5() but drops its chunk_dim checks; read_dataset_typed()'s LatentNeuroVec branch duplicates (incorrectly) load_data(); S3 as.array.LatentNeuroVec duplicates fmrilatent; h5file methods are duplicated across cluster_array.R and cluster_experiment.R and documented as returning the H5File although they return the filename; .get_cluster_data_cached is a stub carrying another helper's roxygen; deprecated make_run_* defer closing onto parent.frame().

title: Performance: O(N) shard appends and per-cluster-per-timepoint reads
description: append_frame_shard_h5() opens every existing shard to check ID collisions, so each append is O(N) in shard count. linear_access() on H5ParcellatedScan issues one HDF5 read per cluster x timepoint and recomputes split() on every call.

title: Frame rollback no longer cleans a store that crashed before its first root manifest
description: Rollback now only removes .manifest-* and shard partials inside a directory whose root manifest validates (so arbitrary directories are never touched). A sharded store that crashed during write_sharded_frame_h5() before committing its first manifest therefore keeps its partials; frame_store_info() reports it as not a store. Consider an explicit marker file written first by write_sharded_frame_h5() so such directories can be proven ours.
